thread.title: Roku Stock Price Target Cut On U.S.-China Trade Tensions | Investor's Business Daily

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Roku Stock Price Target Cut On U.S.-China Trade Tensions | Investor's Business Daily
text:
The U.S.-China trade war is likely to impact sales of Chinese-made televisions in the U.S., crimping growth prospects for streaming video platform Roku ( ROKU ), a Wall Street analyst said Wednesday. She slashed her price target on Roku stock to a new Street low.
X Needham analyst Laura Martin reiterated her buy rating on Roku stock, but cut her price target to 45 from 85. Roku stock fell 1.8% to 35.17 on the stock market today .
"We believe 35%-45% of Roku's total user adds came from Roku-powered, Chinese-made TVs in fiscal 2018, and that TCL was about half of that," Martin said in a report to clients.
Roku licenses a smart TV operating system to television makers, including TCL. Over the weekend, TCL announced that it is selling its consumer-electronics businesses to focus on component technology.

Please contact customer service CLOSE New Roku User Estimate Lowered Martin lowered her estimate for new Roku users in 2019 as well as revenue and earnings based on her outlook for lower sales of Roku-powered, Chinese-made TVs in the U.S. She cut her estimate for new Roku users by nearly 20% to 5 million for 2019. The company ended the third quarter with 23.8 million active accounts, up 43% year over year.
Roku gets most of its revenue from advertising inserted into programming on its platform. It also sells streaming video set-top boxes and dongles, which compete with devices from Alphabet 's ( GOOGL ) Google, Amazon.com ( AMZN ) and Apple ( AAPL ).
"In most quarters, advertising is about two-thirds of Roku's total platform revenue," Martin said. "Of this, about half is video ads and half is endemic advertising by apps promoting their content."
